name: GO Classes CS 2025 | ALL INDIA MOCK TEST 4

question.text:
I am not sure if the bus that has been booked will be able to ______ all the students.

  1. sit
  2. deteriorate
  3. fill
  4. accommodate

Rajiv Gandhi Khel Ratna Award was conferred _______ Mary Kom, a six-time world champion in boxing, recently in a ceremony _______ the Rashtrapati Bhawan (the President’s official residence) in New Delhi.

  1. with, at
  2. on, in
  3. on, at
  4. to, at

Machine $A,$ which produces $15$ golf clubs per hour, fills a production lot in $6$ hours.

Machine $B$ fills the same production lot in $1.5$ hours. How many golf clubs does machine $B$ produce per hour?

  1. $30$
  2. $40$
  3. $60$
  4. $90$

Bernard has wrapped gifts for the $14$ students in his class, and numbered the gifts from $1$ to $14.$

Bernard knows the weight of each gift. After wrapping each gift, Bernard realized that he accidentally dropped his phone in one of the boxes. In order to avoid unwrapping many gifts, he plans to do the following:

  1. Divide the $14$ gifts into $2$ piles, with the smallest $7$ gift numbers in the first pile and the largest $7$ gift numbers in the second pile.
  2. Weigh the first pile. If it is heavier than expected, retain the first pile. Otherwise retain the second pile.
  3. Divide the retained pile into $2$ piles containing as close to the same number of gifts as possible. If there is an odd number of gifts, the first pile will have one fewer gift than the second pile. The smallest gift numbers are in the first pile.
  4. Repeat Steps $2$ and $3$ until the retained pile has a single gift that contains the phone. Open that gift to retrieve the phone.

In which of the following situations would Bernard weigh the fewest number of piles?

  1. The phone is in gift number $3.$
  2. The phone is in gift number $13.$
  3. The phone is in gift number $8.$
  4. The phone is in gift number $6.$

The results of asking $50$ students if they participate in music or sports are shown in the Venn diagram.

What percentage of the $50$ students do not participate in music and do not participate in sports?

  1. $80 \%$
  2. $20 \%$
  3. $70 \%$
  4. $40 \%$

If $x$ satisfies the equation $4^{8^{x}}=256$, then $x$ is equal to __________.

  1. $\frac{1}{2}$ 
  2. $\log _{16} 8$
  3. $\frac{2}{3}$
  4. $\log _{4} 8$

The ratio of zinc and copper in a brass pieces is $13: 7$. How much zinc will be there in $100 \mathrm{~kg}$ of such a piece?

  1. $20 \mathrm{~kg}$
  2. $35 \mathrm{~kg}$
  3. $55 \mathrm{~kg}$
  4. $65 \mathrm{~kg}$
Which figure is identical to the first?

Last year, a magazine charged a $\$ 50$ subscription fee. This year, the price will be increased by $\$ 10$. If the magazine could lose $4$ subscribers this year and still collect the same revenue as it did last year, how many subscribers did the magazine have last year?

  1. $21$
  2. $22$
  3. $23$
  4. $24$

The sequence $S$ is defined by $S_{n}=2\left(S_{n-1}\right)-4$ for each integer $n \geq 2$. If $S_{1}$ $=6$, what is the value of $S_{5}?$

  1. $16$
  2. $20$
  3. $24$
  4. $36$

Consider a binary function $\mathrm{g}: \mathrm{M} \times \mathrm{M} \rightarrow\{$ true, false $\}$, where $\mathrm{M}$ is a non-empty subset of the natural numbers that contains an even number of distinct elements.

Which of the following statements can never be true about $\mathrm{g}$? (Select all that apply)

  1. $\mathrm{g}$ is symmetric and antisymmetric.
  2. $\mathrm{g}$ defines a total order and an equivalence relation.
  3. $\mathrm{g}$ is an injection
  4. $\mathrm{g}$ is antisymmetric but not a surjection

You have $n$ lists, each consisting of $m$ integers sorted in ascending order. Merging these lists into a single sorted list will take time:

  1. $O(nm \log  m)$
  2. $O(mn \log  n)$
  3. $O(m + n)$
  4. $O(mn)$

Which of the following statements is/are true? ( $\otimes$ is XOR operator, $*$ is AND operator)

  1. $a \otimes b$ always equals $(\overline{a} * b)+(a * \overline{b})$
  2. $a \otimes(b \otimes c)$ always equals $(a \otimes b) \otimes c$
  3. $(a+\overline{b}) *(b+c)$ always equals $a+c$

 

  1. III only
  2. I and II only
  3. II and III only
  4. I, II, and III

Consider the following resource allocation graph:

Which of the following is/are correct about the above resource allocation graph?

  1. The current System is in a deadlock.
  2. The current System is in deadlock but adding one more instance of $\text{R1}$ will make the system deadlock-free.
  3. The current System is NOT in a deadlock but if we add an additional process $\text{P4}$ that demands an instance of $\text{R1}$, then the system will go to a deadlock.
  4. The current System is NOT in a deadlock but if $\text{P2}$ additionally demands one instance of $\text{R1}$, then the system will go to a deadlock.

Consider the following lexical analyser “flex” specification -

 

$$\begin{array}{llc} & \begin{array}{l}\text { Regular } \\ \text { Expression }\end{array} & \text { Token } \\ \text { Rule 1 } & \mathrm{c} & \{\text { printf (“ 1 ”);}\; \} \\ \text { Rule 2 } & \mathrm{ac}^{+} \mathrm{b}^{\ast} & \{\text { printf (“ 2 ”);}\; \} \\ \text { Rule 3 } & \mathrm{cc} & \{\text { printf (“ 3 ”);}\; \} \\ \text { Rule 4 } & \mathrm{a}\mathrm{b}^{\ast}  & \{\text { printf (“ 4 ”);}\; \} \\ \text { Rule 5 } & \mathrm{a} & \{\text { printf (“ 5 ”);}\; \} \\ \text { Rule 6 } & \mathrm{a}\mathrm{c}^{\ast}  \mathrm{~b}^{+} & \{\text { printf (“ 6 ”);}\; \}\end{array}$$

When using regular expressions to scan an input, we resolve conflicts by taking the largest possible match at any point.

If two longest matches are of the same length then we give preference in the below order: Rule $1$(Highest Priority), Rule $6$(Lowest Priority).

Which of the following rule(s) can be deleted such that lexer’s behavior does not get changed for any of the input strings?

  1. Rule $3$
  2. Rule $4$
  3. Rule $5$
  4. Rule $6$

Suppose $\text{Z}_1, \text{Z}_2, \text{Z}_3$ are i.i.d. (independently and identically distributed) Bernoulli random variables with parameter $p=\frac{1}{2}$. The random variable $\text{S}=\text{Z}_2 \text{Z}_3$ if $\text{Z}_1=1$, and $\text{S}=\text{Z}_2+\text{Z}_3$ if $\text{Z}_1=0$. Find $\text{P}\left(\text{Z}_1=1 \mid \text{S}=1\right)$.

  1. $1 / 8$
  2. $1 / 3$
  3. $3 / 8$
  4. $1 / 2$

For a pair $(A, B)$ of subsets of the set $X=\{1,2, \ldots, 100\}$, let $A \triangle B$ denote the set of all elements of $X$ which belong to exactly one of $A$ or $B$. The number of pairs $(A, B)$ of subsets of $X$ such that $A \triangle B=\{2,4,6, \ldots, 100\}$ is

  1. $2^{151}$
  2. $2^{102}$
  3. $2^{150}$
  4. $2^{100}$.

Which of the following statements about datagrams sent by a node in a network using $\textsf{IPv4}$ protocol is (are) true?

  1. Datagrams at the source must be the size of the smallest maximum transmission unit (MTU) of all the links on a path to the destination.
  2. Datagrams may be fragmented during routing.
  3. Datagrams are reassembled only at the destination.

 

  1. I only
  2. II only
  3. III only
  4. II and III

If $f(3)=3$ and $f^{\prime}(x) \geq 2$ for $3 \leq x \leq 6$, use the Mean Value Theorem to determine the smallest possible value of $f(6)$.

  1. $2$
  2. $3$
  3. $6$
  4. $9$

Consider the following grammar over the alphabet $\{a, b, d\}$:
$$
\begin{aligned}
& S \rightarrow A B D \\
& A \rightarrow a \mid B S B \\
& B \rightarrow b \mid D \\
& D \rightarrow d \mid \epsilon
\end{aligned}
$$
What is the First set for the non-terminal $S$?
  1. $a, b, d$
  2. $a, b$
  3. $a, d$
  4. $d, \epsilon$

Assume that any $n\text{-bit}$ positive integer $x$ is stored as a linked list of bits so that the first element of the list is the least significant bit. For example, $x=14=1110_2$ is stored as the linked list $(0,1,1,1)$ of size $n=4$.
For this data structure, the operation that replaces $x$ by $\left\lfloor\dfrac{x}{8}\right\rfloor$ can be done in

  1. $\Theta(1)$ steps
  2. $\Theta(\log n)$ steps
  3. $\Theta(n)$ steps
  4. $\Theta(n \log n)$ steps

Say that A is the primary key of table $\mathbf{R}$, and that $B$ is another, numeric attribute of $\mathbf{R}$. Let $r$ be the number of tuples in table $\mathbf{R}$.
$$
\left(\pi_{\mathrm{A}}\left(\sigma_{\mathrm{B}<5}(\mathbf{R})\right)\right) \bowtie\left(\pi_{\mathrm{A}}\left(\sigma_{\mathrm{B} \geq 5}(\mathbf{R})\right)\right)
$$
How many tuples will result from the above RA expression?

  1. $0$
  2. $1$
  3. $\frac{1}{2} r$
  4. $r$

A super-simple RISC-like computer has three main computational elements (memory, registers, and ALU) which it uses to implement the four types of instructions shown below. This chart shows which main computational elements each instruction uses. For example, arithmetic instructions first require accessing memory, then accessing registers, then accessing the ALU, then accessing registers once more.

Suppose these computational elements require the following time to operate and settle (for either read or write operations):

  • Memory: $M$ ns
  • Registers: $R$ ns
  • ALU: $A$ ns

Which of the following statements is/are true?

  1. If the machine has a single-cycle datapath with a constant cycle time, then the cycle cannot be faster than $2 * M+2 * R+A$ ns.
  2. If the machine has a multi-cycle datapath with a constant cycle time, then operations can be pipelined, but the cycle cannot be faster than $\max (\mathrm{M}, \mathrm{R}, \mathrm{A})\; \mathrm{ns}$.
  3. Suppose that the machine has a single-cycle datapath, but the cycle length is varied as follows: Branch and arithmetic instructions will execute in $M+2$ * $R+A$ ns; load instructions will execute in $2 * M+2$ * $R+A$ ns ; store instructions will execute in $2 * M+R+A$ ns. In this case, the throughput will be better than in option I or II above.

 

  1. I only
  2. I and II only
  3. II and III only
  4. I, II, and III

Which of the following problems is/are decidable?
  1. Determining whether two nondeterministic finite automata accept the same language.
  2. Determining whether two context-free grammars represent exactly the same language.
  3. Determining whether a propositional logic expression is satisfiable.
  4. Determining whether a Turing machine will halt for a given input.

Consider the following binary heap.

Suppose that the last operation performed in the binary heap above was inserting the key $x$. What is/are possible values of $x?$

  1. $19$
  2. $26$
  3. $32$
  4. $22$

Consider a machine with a physical memory of $8 \mathrm{~GB}$, a page size of $8 \mathrm{~KB}$, and a page table entry size of $4$ bytes. How many levels of page tables would be required to map a $46$-bit virtual address space if every page table fits into a single page?

Suppose that $\text{X}$ is a random variable where:
$$
\text{P(X}=-3)=1 / 3 \quad \text{P(X}=0)=1 / 3 \quad \text{P(X}=3)=1 / 3 .
$$
and let $\text{Y = X}^2$.
What will be the value of $\text{E[Y]}?$

  1. $6$
  2. $0$
  3. $2 / 3$
  4. $1$

Suppose that process $P$ has been running for several days when a new process $Q$ starts up and begins contending with $P$ for resources. Which of the following is/are true?

  1. In a wait-die system, if $P$ needs a resource held by $Q$, then $P$ waits.
  2. In a wait-die system, if $Q$ needs a resource held by $P,$ then $Q$ waits.
  3. In a wound-wait system, if $P$ needs a resource held by $Q,$ then $Q$ yields and waits.
  4. In a wound-wait system, if $Q$ needs a resource held by $P,$ then $P$ yields and waits.

A certain hard drive rotates at $6000$ rpm . It has $1$ KB per sector and averages $128$ sectors per track. Which of the following statements is/are true?

  1. The average latency of the drive is under $6$ milliseconds.
  2. The burst data rate of the drive is over $10 \mathrm{MB} / \mathrm{sec}$.
  3. The average capacity per track is over $1$ MB.

 

  1. II only
  2. I and II only
  3. II and III only
  4. I, II, and III

Suppose two threads execute the following $\mathrm{C}$ code concurrently, accessing shared variables $\textsf{a, b},$ and $\textsf{c}:$

Initialization

int a = 4;
int b = 0;
int c = 0;

Thread 1

if (a < 0) {
    c = b - a;
} else { 
    c = b + a;
}

Thread 2

b = 10;
a = -3;

You can assume that reads and writes of the variables are atomic, and that the order of statements within each thread is preserved in the code generated by the $\mathrm{C}$ compiler.

Statement $\mathrm{X}=\mathrm{Y} \ast \mathrm{Z}$ reads $\mathrm{Y}$, then reads $\mathrm{Z}$ from memory, performs $\mathrm{Y} \ast \mathrm{Z}$, stores/writes it to memory $\mathrm{X}.$

Which of the following values are possible for $\textsf{c}$ after both threads complete?

  1. $4$
  2. $7$
  3. $14$
  4. $-3$

Consider the following language $L$ over the alphabet $\mathrm{A}=\{0,1\}$.

$L=\left\{w \in A^{*}: w\right.$ does not contain any $1$'s in even positions, where the leftmost is position $1 \}$

The number of states in the minimal deterministic finite state automaton for $L$ is ?? (Write answer $0$ if $L$ is not regular)

A binary single-precision floating point number contains the sequence of bits $\textsf{10001111100000000001000000000000}.$

Information is stored in the following left-to-right order: sign bit, exponent $\textsf{(bias -127 )},$ and mantissa (with an implied unit bit).
Which of the following representations in decimal is equivalent?

  1. $2^{31} *\left(1+2^{-12}\right)$
  2. $-1 * 2^{31} *\left(1+2^{-12}\right)$
  3. $-1 * 2^{-65} *\left(1+2^{-10}\right)$
  4. $-1 * 2^{-96} *\left(1+2^{-11}\right)$

Consider the following initialization of an array and pointer.

char a[] = "abc\0de"; 
char  *p = a ;

Let the system be $32$ bit addressable. The size of int is $4$ bytes and the size of char is $1$ byte.
Which of the following is/are TRUE?

  1. sizeof(a) = 7
  2. sizeof(p) = 4 
  3. sizeof(*p) = 1
  4. strlen(p) = 3

Consider a memory of $32$ blocks (labeled $0$ through $31)$ and a cache of $8$ blocks (labeled $0$ through $7).$

In the following sequence of memory block references from the $\text{CPU},$ beginning from an empty cache, on which reference must the cache layout for a direct-mapped and a $4$-way set associative cache first differ? (i.e. the referenced memory block causes an existing cached block to be evicted from the cache)
$$\begin{array}{|l|l|l|l|l|l|l|l|l|}
\hline \text{order of reference} & 1 & 2 & 3 & 4 & 5 & 6 & 7 & 8 \\
\hline \text{block referenced} & 0 & 15 & 18 & 5 & 1 & 13 & 15 & 26 \\
\hline
\end{array}$$

  1. Reference $5$
  2. Reference $2$
  3. Reference $4$
  4. Reference $6$

#include <stdio.h>
int fun(int *i) {
    *i += 5;
    return 2;
}
int main() {
    int x = 3;
    if ((x == 2) && (fun(&x))) {
        x++;
    }
    x = x + fun(&x);
    printf("%d\n", x);
    return 0;
}

What will be the output for the above program?

Assume Left-to-right operand evaluation for "+" operator.

Consider a system with the following specifications:

  • TLB has a $1$ cycle hit time and a $99 \%$ hit rate
  • The TLB miss penalty (page table lookup time) is $100$ cycles
  • The $\text{L1}$ cache has a hit time of $4$ cycles and a hit rate $80 \%$
  • The miss penalty for $\text{L1}$ cache is $50$ cycles

Assuming TLB and $\text{L1}$ cache accesses do not overlap, what is the average memory access time for the system described above?

  1. $15$ cycles
  2. $16$ cycles
  3. $12$ cycles
  4. $13$ cycles

While solving the system of linear equations, the three elementary row operations on a matrix are as following :

  1. Row Swap: A row within the matrix can be switched with another row.
  2. Row Scaling: Each element in a row can be multiplied by a non-zero constant.
  3. Row Replacement: A row can be replaced by the sum of that row and a multiple of another row.

Which of the following is true regarding the Elementary Row Operations?

  1. Row Swap can be performed by using the other two elementary row operations.
  2. Row Scaling can be performed by using the other two elementary row operations.
  3. Row Replacement can be performed by using the other two elementary row operations.
  4. None of the elementary row operations can be performed using the other two.

Consider the following two statements:

  • S1: Consider an undirected, simple graph $G=(V, E)$ with edge weights $w_{e} \geq 0$ such that $w_{e} eq w_{e^{\prime}}$ for all $e, e^{\prime} \in E, e eq e^{\prime}$. Let $s \in V$ be fixed. Then for all $v \in V$ there is a unique shortest $(s, v)$-path.
     
  • S2: Consider an undirected, simple graph $G=(V, E)$ with edge weights $w_{e} \geq 0$ such that $w_{e} eq w_{e^{\prime}}$ for all $e, e^{\prime} \in E, e eq e^{\prime}$. Then there is a unique minimum spanning tree $T$.

Which of the following is correct?

  1. $\mathbf{S 1}$ is true, but $\mathbf{S} 2$ is false.
  2. $\mathbf{S} 1$ is false, but $\mathbf{S} 2$ is true.
  3. Both $\mathbf{S 1}$ and $\mathbf{S 2}$ are true.
  4. Both $\mathbf{S 1}$ and $\mathbf{S 2}$ are false.

Consider a TCP connection utilizing cumulative acknowledgment and the sliding window protocol. Suppose the sender has most recently transmitted a segment with ACK=500, and then the receiver receives a segment with SEQ=300 containing $50$ bytes of data. How should the receiver respond in this scenario?

  1. Send a segment with $A C K=301$.
  2. Send a segment with $\mathrm{ACK}=350$.
  3. Send a segment with $\mathrm{ACK}=500$.
  4. Send a segment with $A C K=551$.

Consider this circuit.


Suppose that the circuit is initialized by setting input $\text{A} =0$ and $\text{B}=0$, with $\mathrm{C}=0$. Assume that all inputs and outputs are clocked. Which of the following statements is/are true?

  1. After the circuit is initialized, if $\text{A}$ is set to $0$ and $\text{B}$ is set to $1,$ then output $\text{C}$ becomes $1$ in the next clock pulse.
  2. After the circuit is initialized, if $\text{A}$ is set to $1$ and $\text{B}$ is set to $0,$ then output $\text{C}$ becomes $1$ in the next clock pulse.
  3. After the circuit is initialized, if $\text{A}$ is set to $1$ and $\text{B}$ is set to $1,$ then output $\text{C}$ becomes $1$ in the next clock pulse.

 

  1. II only
  2. III only
  3. II and III only
  4. I, II, and III

Given a graph $G$ with vertex set $V$ and edge set $E$, which of the following is/are true if and only if $G$ is a tree?

  1. For all vertices $u$ and $v \in V$, there exists a unique simple path from $u$ to $v$.
  2. $G$ is connected, but if any edge $e \in E$ is removed, the resulting graph is not connected.
  3. $G$ is acyclic, but if any edge $e \notin E$ is added, the resulting graph is not acyclic.
  4. $|E|=|V|-1$ and either $G$ is acyclic or $G$ is connected.

A function returns a two's-complement two-byte integer. On success, the return value exceeds $1024.$ On error, the return value is in the range $-1$ through $-10$ to represent ten different error conditions.

Which of the following hexadecimals could not be returned by this function? (Select all that apply)

  1. $\textsf{0401}$
  2. $\textsf{03F0}$
  3. $\textsf{FFED}$
  4. $\textsf{FFF6}$

The intent of the function below is to delete the last node of the list.

void removeLast(Node* first) {
    Node *p, *q;
    p = first;
    q = p->next;
    while (q->next != NULL) {
        p = q;
        q = q->next;
    }
    p->next = NULL;
    free(q);
}

Which of the following describes the class of all linked lists for which this function works correctly?

  1. No linked lists
  2. All non-empty linked lists
  3. All linked lists with more than one node
  4. The empty list and all linked lists with more than one node

Assume that an int variable takes $4$ bytes and a char variable takes $1$ byte. What is the output of the code below?

int main()
{
    int arr[]={10,20,30,40,50,60};
    int *ptr1=arr;
    int *ptr2=arr+5;
    printf("Number of elements between two pointer are: %d.", 
    (ptr2 - ptr1));
    printf("Number of bytes between two pointer are: %d.", 
    (char*)ptr2 - (char*)ptr1);
}
  1. Number of elements between two pointer are: $5$. Number of bytes between two pointers are: $20$
  2. Number of elements between two pointer are: $20.$ Number of bytes between two pointers are: $20$
  3. Number of elements between two pointer are: $5.$ Number of bytes between two pointers are: $5$
  4. Compile time error

Consider the following functional dependencies in a database.
$$\mathrm{AB} \rightarrow \mathrm{DE}, \mathrm{C} \rightarrow \mathrm{E}, \mathrm{D} \rightarrow \mathrm{C}, \text{and}\; \mathrm{E} \rightarrow \mathrm{A}$$
The relation $\text{R(A, B, C, E)}$ is

  1. in second normal form but not in third normal form
  2. in third normal form but not in BCNF
  3. in BCNF
  4. not in second normal form

The routing table below uses the longest prefix match in its routing decisions.
$$
\begin{array}{|c|c|}
\hline \text{Network Address/Length} & \text{Next Hop} \\
\hline \hline 196.94 .8 .0 / 21 & \text{S} \\
\hline 196.94 .16 .0 / 24 & \text{T} \\
\hline 196.94 .0 .0 / 16 & \text{U} \\
\hline
\end{array}
$$
What are the next hops for each of the following two destination addresses?

$\begin{array}{lcc} & \text { Next Hop to } & \text { Next Hop to } \\ & \underline{196.94 .10 .7} & \underline{196.94 .34 .9} \\ \text {(A)} & \text{S} & \text{T} \\ \text {(B)} & \text{S} & \text{U} \\ \text {(C)} & \text{T} & \text{T} \\ \text {(D)} & \text{T} & \text{U} \end{array}$

In a network graph $G=(V, E)$, each edge $e \in E$ has a probability $p_{e}$ of successful transmission. Given two vertices $s \neq t \in V$, your goal is to find the $s$ - $t$ path with the highest probability of successful transmission.

To achieve this, you construct a new graph $G^{\prime}=\left(V^{\prime}, E^{\prime}\right)$ with $V^{\prime}=V$ and $E^{\prime}=E$, and assign weights to edges in $G^{\prime}$ so that finding the shortest path in $G^{\prime}$ using Dijkstra's algorithm will correspond to finding the highest probability path in $G$.

Which of the following could be appropriate weights for edge $e$ in $G^{\prime}$ if its probability in $G$ is $p_{e}$? (Select all that apply.)

  1. $p_{e}$
  2. $\log \left(p_{e}\right)$
  3. $\log \left(\frac{1}{p_{e}}\right)$ or $-\log \left(p_{e}\right)$
  4. $p_{e}^{2}$

Which of the following languages over the alphabet $\mathrm{A}=\{0,1\}$ is/are not regular?

  1. $\left\{w \in A^{*}: w\right.$ contains equal numbers of $1's$ and $0 's \}$
  2. $\left\{w \in A^{*}: w\right.$ contains a prime number of $1 's \}$
  3. $\left\{w \in A^{*}: \exists u \in A^{*}\right.$ such that $\left.w=u u\right\}$
  4. $\left\{\mathrm{w} \in \mathrm{A}^{*}: \exists \mathrm{u} \in \mathrm{A}^{*}\right.$ such that $\left.\mathrm{u}=\mathrm{ww}\right\}$

A certain function $g: N \times N \rightarrow N$ is defined as follows for $x$ and $y \geq 0$ :
\begin{cases}g(0, y)=y+1 & \text { for } y \geq 0 \\ g(x, 0)=g(x-1,1) & \text { for } x>0 \\ g(x, y)=g(x-1, g(x, y-1)) & \text { for } x \text { and } y>0\end{cases}
Which of the following statements is/are true?

  1. $g(1, n)=n-3$
  2. $g(2, n)=2 n-3$
  3. $g(3, n)=2^{n+3}-3$

 

  1. III only
  2. II and III only
  3. I, II, and III
  4. None of the above

Consider the following function.

Function EXPL( int n ) {
    if ( n <= 2 ) then return 1
    return EXPL( n / 2 ) * lg( n )
}

What does EXPL ( n ) return, if $n$ is a power of $2?$

  1. $\lg (n)$
  2. $n * \lg (n)$
  3. $n!* \lg (n)$
  4. $(\lg (n))!$

Suppose the $4000$ -byte IP packet run into a link of MTU $= 1500$ bytes first and then a link of MTU $=900$ bytes next. What is TRUE about fragments sent out on the MTU $=900$ bytes link?

  1. All Fragments has same ID number
  2. There will be total $6$ fragments
  3. Offset of last fragment will be $3840$
  4. Total length of first, third and fifth fragments are same

Consider these $2$ statements -

  • $\text{S1}:$ If $\text{A}$ is invertible, then $\text{A}$ and $\text{A}^{-1}$ have the same eigenvectors.
  • $\text{S2}:$ If $\text{A}$ is invertible, then $\text{A}$ and $\text{A}^{-1}$ have the same eigenvalues.

Which of the following is the correct option?

  1. $\text{S1}$ is correct but $\text{S2}$ is incorrect
